title: Effects of Lactobacillus crispatus-Containing Probiotics and Metformin on Insulin Resistance, Inflammation, and Gut Microbiome in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Protocol for an Open-Label Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) affects 9% to 12% of reproductive-age women worldwide, with higher prevalence reported in India. Its pathophysiology involves insulin resistance, hyperandrogenism, and chronic low-grade inflammation, increasingly linked to gut dysbiosis and lipopolysaccharide-driven toll-like receptor 4 signaling. Elevated calprotectin and suppressed acylated ghrelin (AGH) reflect this inflammatory-metabolic disruption. While metformin remains standard therapy, it does not addres...

title: Metabolic, enzymatic, and probiotic profiling of Lactococcus lactis LBM15: inhibition of Staphylococcus aureus biofilm and virulence genes, and GPR-based prediction.
abstract: This study characterized a Lactococcus lactis strain (LBM15) isolated from traditional yogurt and evaluated its probiotic, antimicrobial, and anti-biofilm attributes, along with its physiological robustness and safety-associated characteristics. The isolate was identified by 16S rRNA sequencing (99% similarity) and exhibited a carbohydrate utilization pattern typical of dairy L. lactis, including efficient fermentation of common hexoses and β-glucosides. Enzymatic profiling revealed high phospha...

title: Psychobiotics: A Paradigm Shift in Dermatological Disorders.
abstract: Recent clinical studies have demonstrated an intricate bidirectional system in the gut-brain-skin axis. Here, the gut microbiome plays dual roles: it can act as a pathological factor while also serving as a potential therapeutic target in psychodermatology. Chronic skin conditions (CSCs) like acne vulgaris, atopic dermatitis, and psoriasis are some of the leading skin problems. Besides that, these conditions are not only associated with anxiety and depression but also result in a drastic decline...

title: Biotransformation of bioactive profiles and metabolomic remodeling of germinated brown rice milk fermented with probiotic Lactiplantibacillus plantarum.
abstract: This study aimed to isolate, molecularly characterize, and apply multifunctional probiotic lactic acid bacteria (LAB) from traditional Thai fermented sources (dough balls and Khao Mak) to formulate bioactively enriched fermented germinated brown rice milk (FGBRM) using indigenous rice cultivars (Maled Fai, Red Jasmine, and KDML105). From 111 isolates, 59 LAB were identified, including nine exhibiting high amylolytic activity. Lactiplantibacillus plantarum KM7 and KM4 exhibited broad-spectrum ant...

title: Beyond live probiotics: bioactivities, mechanisms, and application perspectives of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus cell-free supernatants.
abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus is one of the most widely investigated probiotic species. Live preparations can modulate intestinal microbiota, support immune function, and ameliorate metabolic disorders. However, poor stability during processing and storage, low gastrointestinal survival, variable intestinal colonization, and potential risks in immunocompromised individuals limit the use of live preparations. Therefore, an increasing number of studies have focused on cell-free supernatant (CFS). S...

title: A multivariate PCA-based evaluation of betaine, vitamin C, and phytogenic (STRESS-BIOMax) - supplemented drinking water in broilers?
abstract: Physiological and metabolic disturbances can impair growth and oxidative balance in broilers. This study evaluated the effects of Stress-BioMax (SBM) supplementation in drinking water (0.00, 0.25, 0.50, and 1.00 mL/L) on growth performance, carcass traits, biochemical indices, oxidative status, and systemic physiological responses. SBM is a drinking-water additive containing betaine, vitamin C, and herbal extracts. Principal component analysis (PCA), quadratic regression, and segmented regressio...

title: Chickpea flour (Cicer arietinum L) improves viability of potentially probiotics Lactobacillus plantarum S180.7 and Lactobacillus plantarum SBR64.7 in milk-based formulations.
abstract: This study evaluated the effect of adding chickpea flour to milk-based formulations on physicochemical parameters, the survival, and viability of potentially probiotic microorganisms. Four formulations were prepared using skimmed milk (10%) and sucrose (10%), each containing Lactobacillus plantarum S180.7 (CF1) or L. plantarum SBR64.7 (CF2), with or without 4.5% chickpea flour (TF1 and TF2). Composition, physicochemical properties, total phenolic content, antioxidant activity, and bacterial viab...

title: Probiotic Extracellular Vesicles: Bridging Lacticaseibacillus casei and the Intestinal Epithelium.
abstract: The mechanisms underlying the health benefits of probiotics remain incompletely understood. Among the proposed mediators, bacterial extracellular vesicles (EVs) have been proposed as mediators of interkingdom communication between probiotic bacteria and their hosts. In this study, we show that Lacticaseibacillus casei BL23 releases higher EV levels during late stationary phase, with a predominant population of ∼113 nm. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) confirmed the ultrastructural morphology o...

title: Lacticaseibacillus paracasei INIA P708: a safe human isolate with probiotic and technological potential.
abstract: Lacticaseibacillus paracasei INIA P708 was isolated from breast-fed infant feces. It stood out by its stable ropy phenotype, which could indicate exopolysaccharide (EPS) production and antimicrobial properties. Bearing in mind its potential use in the food chain, the objective of this work was to study L. paracasei INIA P708 potential probiotic traits, and technological and safety characteristics, in comparison to the commercial probiotic L. rhamnosus GG strain. A full genomic analysis was also ...

title: Super-resolution mapping of nuclear stress signaling by probiotic-derived extracellular vesicles in UV-induced skin photodamage.
abstract: Ultraviolet (UV)-induced photodamage drives oxidative stress, DNA damage, and chronic inflammation, leading to progressive cellular ultrastructure and skin function degeneration. Despite the potential of probiotics as anti-photodamage agents, their nanoscale action mechanism remains unexplored. Here, we utilize super-resolution fluorescence microscopy to investigate the cellular and molecular basis of Lactobacillus plantarum-derived extracellular vesicles (L. plantarum EVs) in mitigating photoda...

title: Physicochemical and Sensory Properties of Probiotic Fermented Sheep Milk Fortified with Inulin and Sodium Butyrate.
abstract: Background/Objectives: In the production of functional foods, bioactive compounds are commonly incorporated into the product, including dietary fibre, polyols, probiotics and prebiotics, unsaturated fatty acids, vitamins, minerals, and other health-promoting constituents. Such ingredients are used, among others, for the fortification of dairy products. title: Effects of Acute Ecklonia cava Supplementation on Submaximal Cycling and Repeated-Sprint Performance in Trained Cyclists: A Randomised Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Crossover Trial.
abstract: This study examined whether acute Ecklonia cava (EC) ingestion altered physiological responses during submaximal cycling or power output during subsequent repeated maximal sprints in experienced male cyclists.

title: Food-Grade Metal-Phenolic Network and Polysaccharide Microencapsulation Enhances the In Vivo Anti-Colitic Efficacy of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum B112.
abstract: Probiotic therapy for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) has a persistent practical obstacle: most cells given by mouth die before they reach the colon.

title: Impact of Probiotic Intervention on Lymphocyte Activity in Mice Challenged with Pea Albumins (Pisum sativum L.).
abstract: Background: Probiotics are microorganisms with proven health benefits in humans. However, the mechanisms underlying the direct effects of these compounds on immune cells remain unclear. This study aimed to examine the effects of probiotics on immunity in mice exposed to allergenic dietary proteins, specifically pea albumin (PA). We hypothesized that probiotics would alter lymphocyte activity, leading to measurable differences in the immune response to these proteins. Methods: The relationship be...

title: Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 Attenuates Hyperoxia-Induced Lung Injury in a Newborn Rat Model.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity in preterm infants, and effective preventive strategies are lacking. This study investigated the protective effect of orally administered Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 in a neonatal rat model of hyperoxia-induced lung injury. Methods: Newborn Sprague-Dawley rat pups were randomly allocated to normoxia control (NC), hyperoxia control (HC), and hyperoxia with probiotic supplementation (HP) groups. ...

title: Effects of Functional Yogurt Supplementation on Aflatoxin-Induced Maternal-Fetal Toxicity in Pregnant Rats.
abstract: Aflatoxin (AF) exposure during pregnancy may compromise maternal health and fetal development. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of gestational exposure to AF in pregnant Wistar rats and the mitigating effect of a functional yogurt (FY) containing inactivated biomass of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus and Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Animals were exposed to total AF (sum AFB1, AFB2, AFG1 and AFG2: 1.0 mg/kg/day) from gestational day (GD) 6 to 15, with or without FY supplementation. Maternal and...

title: Chlorella for health: evidence from a GRADE-assessed systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis.
abstract: Chlorella species have attracted attention for their potential to improve cardiovascular and metabolic health; however, comprehensive evidence from controlled trials remains limited.

title: Gastric microbiota‑derived postbiotics as antimicrobial and anti‑biofilm agents.
abstract: The human gastric microbiota is recognized as a diverse and metabolically active ecosystem with significant roles in health and disease. Beyond probiotics, postbiotics, non-viable microbial products with antimicrobial and anti-biofilm properties, offer stable and safer therapeutic alternatives. Rising antimicrobial resistance and biofilm associated infections caused by pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus and Candida albicans highlight the urgent need for new strategies. Based on this evidenc...

title: Biosynthesis of 3-Hydroxy-3-methylbutyrate by Probiotic Escherichia coli Nissle 1917.
abstract: 3-Hydroxy-3-methylbutyrate (HMB) is an important nutritional supplement for managing sarcopenia. This study engineered an HMB biosynthetic pathway in the probiotic Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN). The initial engineered strain exhibited low HMB titers, as carbon flux was primarily diverted toward acetate formation. journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: High CLA-producing Lactiplantibacillus plantarum MNN1 alleviates irritable bowel syndrome through activation of intestinal PPARα signaling pathway.
abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common gut-brain axis disorder characterized by visceral hypersensitivity, abdominal pain, and anxiety. Although probiotics have emerged as a promising strategy for IBS management, the specific metabolite-driven mechanisms and their role in gut-brain axis modulation remain largely unclear. title: Genomic and functional characterization of Bacillus siamensis AFSC23 isolated from the gut of European conger (Conger conger) as a probiotic candidate for aquaculture.
abstract: The intestinal microbiota of fish represents a valuable source of antimicrobial and health-promoting bacteria. In this context, we report for the first time the isolation of Bacillus siamensis strain AFSC23 from the intestine of Conger conger. The strain was comprehensively characterized using an integrated genomic and functional approach to assess its safety and probiotic potential in aquaculture. title: Synthetic Biology Toolbox for Lactiplantibacillus plantarum: Engineering Next-Generation Probiotic Cell Factories.
abstract: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum has emerged as a promising synthetic biology chassis owing to its food-grade safety, probiotic properties, and adaptability to the gastrointestinal tract. Its engineering potential has expanded rapidly in live biotherapeutics, functional foods, biosensors, and animal health. However, its broader application is still limited by the lack of standardized genetic parts, versatile engineering tools, and industrially compatible chassis. This review summarizes recent advan...

title: Large-Scale Comparative Genomics of 1,374 Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Genomes Reveals an Open Pan-genome and Strain-Level Variation in Probiotic-Associated and Safety-Related Genomic Features.
abstract: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum is widely studied for food fermentation and probiotic applications, but its functional and safety-related characteristics are strongly strain dependent. Large-scale comparative genomics can characterize this diversity and support genome-informed strain prioritization, although genomic evidence alone does not establish probiotic efficacy or safety. A RefSeq genome collection of L. plantarum was subjected to accession-level auditing, exact-sequence dereplication, and ...

title: Subcritical Water in Antimicrobial Benzyl Isothiocyanate Nanoemulsions Preparation and Formulation: A Novel Green Approach for Enhanced Bio-Functionality and Dietary Supplements.
abstract: Benzyl isothiocyanate (BITC) is mainly found in vegetable and fruit seeds with unique biological properties such as anti-cancer and antimicrobial properties. But BITC in pharmaceutical and food formulations faces various challenges, such as low water solubility, environmental instability, and heat sensitivity. This study developed a method based on subcritical water (SW) to prepare BITC nanoemulsion (NE) with desirable activities. Using xanthan and Arabic gums as stabilizers and Tween 80 (T 80) ...

title: Disrupting Salmonella colonization and resistance: probiotic cell-free supernatants inhibit biofilm formation and invasion in meat and human isolates.
abstract: Salmonella enterica remains a paramount global public health threat due to the rapid emergence of multi-drug and pan-drug resistant (PDR) strains transmitted through the food supply chain. This study adopted a One Health cross-sectional framework to investigate the occurrence and biocontrol of PDR Salmonella enterica serovars (S. Enteritidis, S. Kentucky, and S. Anatum) isolated from clinical gastroenteritis cases and retail meat products in Egypt.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: Probiotics as a Strategy for Mitigating Viral Infections in Poultry: Immunomodulatory Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.
abstract: Poultry viral infections remain a persistent challenge for the poultry industry, causing significant economic losses and posing potential threats to human health. The escalating frequency of outbreaks involving pathogens, such as infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), Newcastle disease virus (NDV) and avian influenza virus (AIV), underscores the urgent need for effective interventions. title: Effects of Body-Mass-Scaled Protein and Leucine Supplementation on Body Composition and Cardiometabolic Blood Markers During Weight Loss in Older Men-A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background: Overweight and obesity are burgeoning health epidemics. Diets including alternate-day fasting (ADF) promote weight loss but risk significant muscle loss, posing health implications to seniors at risk of sarcopenia. Leucine, the key muscle protein synthesis (MPS) driver, effectively stimulates MPS with lower calorie intake than protein. title: Bioprospecting of Cheese Whey: Isolation, Safety and Cytoprotective Effects of Limosilactobacillus fermentum Strains on Intestinal Cells.
abstract: Bioprospecting is the identification and exploitation of natural resources for commercial purposes. Cheese whey is a major dairy by-product rich in nutrients and a possible source of bioactive compounds. The aim of this study was to isolate and identify lactic acid bacteria from cheese whey and characterize them based on their probiotic and technological properties, together with their cytotoxicity and cytoprotective effect on intestinal epithelial cells. From 142 isolates, three were selected a...

title: Insights into the Health-Promoting Properties and Nutraceutical and Food Applications of Lonicera japonica Thunb.
abstract: Lonicera japonica Thunb. (L. japonica), an edible medicinal plant that has been widely consumed in East Asian countries, including China, Japan, and Korea, for centuries, has long been regarded as a superior herb in traditional Chinese medicine and is an economically important crop commonly used in beverages, foods, and herbal medicines. title: In vitro assessment of the probiotic potential and safety of lactic acid bacteria for aquatic animal health.
abstract: This study evaluated the in vitro probiotic-related properties and preliminary safety profiles of five lactic acid bacteria (LAB) strains for potential use in aquaculture: Limosilactobacillus reuteri ATCC 55730, Lentilactobacillus kefiri K107, Latilactobacillus sakei SN34, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum FI8595, and Streptococcus thermophilus BioSt64. title: Modulation of Early-Life Calf Gut Microbiota by Bacteriocin-Producing Lactiplantibacillus pentosus AA86 and Pediococcus pentosaceus AA94.
abstract: Early-life gut microbiota plays a critical role in livestock health and productivity. Probiotic interventions, particularly those employing bacteriocin-producing lactic acid bacteria (LAB), may contribute to modulation of microbial development during this critical period. This study evaluated Lactiplantibacillus pentosus AA86 (formerly Lactobacillus pentosus) and Pediococcus pentosaceus AA94 for genomic safety, bacteriocin potential, and their effects on calf gut microbiota. Whole-genome sequenc...

title: Impact of probiotic supplementation on serum klotho levels and inflammatory status in patients with diabetic kidney disease.
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) involves complex metabolic and inflammatory pathways, where gut dysbiosis via the gut-kidney axis plays a critical pathophysiological role. Probiotics may resolve renal decline and modulate aging biomarkers, but clinical evidence in DKD remains limited. This study evaluated the effects of Lactobacillus supplementation on serum alpha-Klotho levels, systemic inflammation, and renal biomarkers DKD patients. In an open-label, parallel-group controlled clinical trial, co...

title: Performance evaluation of Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) fed diets supplemented with Lactobacillus plantarum, Bacillus subtilis and Candida infanticola.
abstract: Aquaculture is the fastest-growing agricultural activity globally, providing healthy food with comparatively low environmental impact. However, high stocking densities can generate excessive organic matter, causing stress and increasing pathogen susceptibility in fish. This study evaluated the effects of dietary supplementation with Candida infanticola UFSJ7A, Bacillus subtilis ATCC 19,659, and Lactobacillus plantarum UFSJP2 on Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) performance, intestinal morphol...
journal: Brazilian journal of microbiology : [publication of the Brazilian Society for Microbiology]

title: Inhibitory effect of Lacticaseibacillus paracasei VCare-360 on Candida albicans in mice with vaginal candidiasis.
abstract: Vaginal candidiasis (VC), mainly triggered by Candida species, ranks among the most‑common reproductive‑tract infections worldwide. Over‑utilization of antibiotics and antifungal medicines aggravates fungal drug‑resistance, which makes it imperative to explore novel alternative therapies. This work intended to investigate the anti‑Candida‑albicans activity of Lacticaseibacillus paracasei VCare‑360.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: Lactobacillus plantarum may prevent cholesterol gallstone formation by restoring gallbladder motility through preserving Cajal-like cells in mice.
abstract: Gallstone disease is closely linked to gallbladder dysmotility and gut microbiota dysbiosis; however, the specific role of Lactobacillus depletion in this pathogenesis remains unclear. This study investigated whether lithogenic diet (LD) induced cholesterol gallstone formation is associated with Lactobacillus deficiency and evaluated the potential of Lactobacillus plantarum (L. plantarum) supplementation to mitigate stone formation by restoring gallbladder motility.

title: Mitigation of perfluorooctanoic acid immunotoxicity in Ruditapes philippinarum haemocytes by Lactobacillus plantarum Ps-8.
abstract: As an emerging pollutant, perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) poses potential risks to the immune systems of bivalves. While probiotic supplementation has been shown in aquaculture to mitigate pollutant-induced harm, its ability to modulate PFOA immunotoxicity in bivalves remains unclear. In this study, Ruditapes philippinarum was exposed to PFOA (0.2 or 20 μg/L) for six days, with or without dietary supplementation of the probiotic Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Ps-8 (10⁶ CFU/mL). Results indicated th...

title: Synbiotic supplementation leads to gut microbiome communities with functional capacity linked to better brain white matter development in preterm infants.
abstract: Preterm birth, a major cause of brain injury, is often linked to dysregulated gut microbiome development. This association underscores microbial metabolic function as a modifiable target to support neurodevelopment. In this secondary analysis of data derived from a randomized controlled trial (Trial Registration: ISRCTN96620855), we tested whether daily nutritional supplementation with Bifidobacterium breve M-16V, short- and long-chain oligosaccharides, and L-glutamine could steer the gut microb...

title: Potassium-increasing regimens in patients at high risk of ventricular arrhythmias: a prespecified observational analysis of the randomized POTCAST trial.
abstract: The POTCAST trial (n = 1200) showed that targeting high-normal plasma potassium levels reduced ventricular arrhythmias in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs). We compared changes in plasma potassium and described outcomes across the three regimens used to increase plasma potassium.
journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

title: Probiotics supplements on fattening guinea pigs: effects on carcass traits and non-carcass components.
abstract: The growing demand for animal protein is driving the search for natural alternatives, such as probiotics, following the ban on growth-promoting antibiotics due to bacterial resistance. The objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of including probiotics made from agro-industrial waste fermented with Lactobacillus acidophilus and Kluyveromyces fragilis and their combination on carcass traits, non-carcass components and colour and pH evolution during muscle-to-meat conversion of 90-day-o...

title: Modulating stress and sleep through a multi-compound dietary supplement: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
abstract: Stress and poor sleep are prevalent public health concerns that negatively impact well-being and daily functioning. Although adaptogens and sleep-focused supplements have separately demonstrated potential benefits, few studies have examined combined effects, particularly in healthy populations. Therefore, this study evaluated the impact of morning adaptogens, evening sleep-focused supplements, and their combination on stress, mood, and subjective and objective sleep quality.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Valorization of Citrus limetta peel powder for probiotic encapsulation: enhanced gastrointestinal and storage stability of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum RAD1 isolated from fermented radish (Raphanus sativus L.).
abstract: Probiotics offer significant health benefits when consumed in adequate amounts; however, their viability is often compromised during processing, storage, and transit through the gastrointestinal tract, which limits their effectiveness in functional food applications. In the present study, seventeen indigenous LAB strains were isolated from fermented radish, among which six strains showed potential probiotic characteristics. title: Effects of Post-infection Supplementation with Lactiplantibacillus plantarum CRD7 and Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus CRD11 on Helicobacter pylori Virulence Gene Expression in a Rat Model of Gastric Infection.
abstract: Helicobacter pylori infects nearly half of the global population and causes gastritis through virulence factors such as CagA and VacA. Increasing antibiotic resistance has reduced the effectiveness of conventional eradication therapies, highlighting the need for alternative strategies, including probiotics. title: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG enhances gefitinib efficacy and reduces treatment-related toxicity via propionyl-L-carnitine regulation.
abstract: Gefitinib improves outcomes in patients with EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer; however, treatment-related gastrointestinal and hepatic toxicity can limit its long-term use. Here, we investigate whether probiotic strains can improve gefitinib efficacy while reducing treatment-associated toxicity. Among the tested strains, Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) shows the strongest enhancement of gefitinib efficacy while reducing intestinal and hepatic injury without altering systemic gefitini...

title: Genomic and functional characterization of Limosilactobacillus fermentum DX2034 identifies a probiotic candidate with TLR2-associated anti-adipogenic activity.
abstract: Limosilactobacillus fermentum is a promising probiotic species with reported benefits for gastrointestinal health and host metabolism. In this study, a novel L. fermentum strain, DX2034, isolated from the feces of a healthy Korean infant, was characterized through phenotypic and genomic analyses, and its anti-adipogenic activity was evaluated in differentiated 3T3-L1 adipocytes. DX2034 exhibited high tolerance to simulated gastric and bile conditions and showed stronger adhesion to Caco-2 cells ...

title: Probiotic Intervention With Bacillus coagulans and Lactobacillus acidophilus in Small Animals Experimental Ulcerative Colitis: Insights From a Small Animal Model.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease is a significant health concern not only in humans but also in companion animals and livestock, where it manifests as chronic diarrhoea, abdominal pain, and mucosal injury. Probiotics have gained increasing attention as potential therapeutic agents due to their immunomodulatory effects and ability to restore intestinal homeostasis. This study investigated the therapeutic efficacy of Bacillus coagulans and Lactobacillus acidophilus in an acetic acid-induced ulcerative c...

title: Exploring whole-genome analysis of a gamma-aminobutyric acid -producing marine Lactiplantibacillus plantarum: genomic insights into neuroactive and probiotic potential.
abstract: GABA-producing lactic acid bacteria are gaining attention as psychobiotics capable of influencing the microbiota-gut-brain axis, yet marine-derived strains remain poorly characterized. Here, the complete genomic characterization is reported for the marine strain Lactiplantibacillus plantarum EI6, focusing on its probiotic potential, GABA production, and safety. title: Oral KCl Supplementation Safely Reduces Body Na+ Surplus and Blood Pressure.
abstract: Potassium-enriched table salt lowers blood pressure (BP) and reduces cardiovascular mortality. Whether these beneficial effects stem from reduced Na+ intake, increased K+ intake, or both is unknown. We tested the hypothesis that oral potassium chloride (KCl) supplementation lowers body Na+ content and BP in patients with essential hypertension (EH) or hyperaldosteronism, independent of salt intake.

title: Compatibility of toothpastes with probiotics for periodontal health: an in vitro and ex vivo study.
abstract: Dental biofilms are associated with oral diseases such as periodontitis, peri-implantitis, halitosis, and tooth decay. These diseases are characterized by dysbiosis, an imbalance between the host and microbiome. Current treatments rely on the mechanical removal of the biofilm and suppressing the microbiome with broad spectrum antimicrobials. title: A Dominant Probiotic from the Traditional Chinese Fermented Food Douzhier Exhibits Anti-Influenza Activity.
abstract: Background: Douzhier, a traditional Chinese fermented food with a history spanning over 1000 years, harbors a complex community of beneficial microbiota. In this study, we isolated Lactococcus lactis subsp. cremoris (designated L. cremoris D2022), one of the dominant bacterial species in Douzhier, and evaluated its efficacy against influenza A virus (IAV) infection. title: Effects of Curcumin Supplementation on Inflammatory Biomarkers in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Chronic low-grade inflammation contributes to the pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated randomized evidence on the effects of oral curcumin or curcuminoid supplementation on circulating inflammatory biomarkers in adults with T2DM.
